text: Of David. To you, LORD, I lift up my soul.
My God, in you I trust; let me not be put to shame, and let my enemies not gloat over me.
Yes, none who wait for you will be put to shame; but those who betray without cause will be put to shame.

versions.text: No one who waits for you will be put to shame; shame belongs to those who betray without cause.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew repeats the same verb (יֵבֹשׁוּ) in both halves, creating a deliberate contrast; the paraphrase 'shame belongs to' loses this parallel echo, which is especially valuable for oral reading. The opening גַּם ('yes, indeed') is also unrepresented.

text: Show me your ways, LORD; teach me your paths.
Lead me in your truth and teach me, for you are the God of my salvation; for you I wait all day long.
Remember your mercy, LORD, and your steadfast love, for they are from of old.
Do not remember the sins of my youth or my rebellions; according to your steadfast love remember me, for the sake of your goodness, LORD.

versions.text: Do not remember the sins of my youth or my rebellions; remember me according to your love, for the sake of your goodness, LORD.
versions.explanation: חֶסֶד is rendered 'steadfast love' in verse 6; keeping the same wording here preserves the psalm's internal consistency. Fronting the phrase also mirrors the Hebrew word order and improves the spoken cadence.

text: Good and upright is the LORD; therefore he instructs sinners in the way.
He guides the humble in what is right and teaches the humble his way.
All the paths of the LORD are love and faithfulness for those who keep his covenant and his testimonies.
For the sake of your name, LORD, forgive my guilt, for it is great.
Who is the one who fears the LORD? He will instruct him in the way he should choose.
He will live out his days in prosperity, and his offspring will inherit the land.
The LORD confides in those who fear him, and he makes his covenant known to them.
My eyes are always on the LORD, for he will pull my feet out of the net.
Turn to me and have mercy on me, for I am alone and afflicted.
The troubles of my heart have multiplied; bring me out of my distresses.

versions.text: The troubles of my heart have grown wide; bring me out of my distress.
versions.explanation: 'Have grown wide' is awkward English and unclear when read aloud; 'have multiplied' conveys the sense of the verb naturally. Also, מְצוּקוֹתַי is plural.

text: See my affliction and my toil, and take away all my sins.
See how many my enemies are, and with what violent hatred they hate me.
Guard my soul and deliver me; let me not be put to shame, for I take refuge in you.
May integrity and uprightness watch over me, for I wait for you.
Redeem Israel, O God, out of all its troubles.
